slides.h: Every row the conclusion rests on failed
b: 77 rows audited, 48 check out — 62%.
The 7 load-bearing rows all fail. The arithmetic is sound almost everywhere; the argument fails exactly where the mission needed it.

slides.h: Audited the papers, then rebuilt the theory ourselves
b: 4 published papers checked equation by equation against their own sources.
Then an in-house strict model with derived transfer functions — not the authors' words — and a confrontation with real data.
The most generous stack we could justify lands 10,000 to 100,000 times below the all-galaxy floor.

floor.label: Best possible all-galaxy floor
floor.note: theoretical best; no instrument achieves it

slides.k: Read this before the verdict lands
slides.h: That gap is not a measurement
b: Our number is a ceiling, from assumptions chosen to flatter the theory.
The floor is a theoretical best case — every galaxy counted, no noise. No instrument achieves it.
So the effect is too small to matter. It is not that our telescopes are too weak.

slides.h: The two core papers contradict each other
b: The later paper disavows the foundation the earlier one's bounce is built on.
And the averaging step — the known critique target — is never derived in either. It is asserted by citation, and the whole magnitude rests on it.

slides.h: The chain held, and the erratum did not
b: 4 gates, 4 passes, every receipt rerunning byte-identical.
The erratum was chased through 8 routes and never found — but the chase won the published Elsevier text of the original, a better source than we had.

slides.h: Alive as a question, finished as a detection program
b: As a personal research interest it is intact and still interesting.
As something to detect, it is done at present sensitivity — and the next honest move is not a bigger stack.
